title: Product search is SQL-injectable
description: The q query parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE expression. An unauthenticated caller can alter the WHERE clause and retrieve products outside the intended search (and potentially exploit SQLite expression injection).
evidence: products.py:40-43 constructs SQL with "... LIKE '%" + q + "%' ...". GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned the full catalogue (all six products) rather than a matching result.

title: Admin review report concatenates display names into SQL
description: The customer's display_name, which is user-controlled through PATCH /account, is interpolated into the report query. A customer can set a quote-containing display name and cause SQL syntax/injection when staff later view the report; the report should use a bound parameter.
evidence: admin.py:77-81 uses f"WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}' ..." instead of a parameterized value. display_name is updated from request data at auth.py:116-125.

title: Review bodies are rendered as stored XSS
description: Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review body text, which is persisted without sanitization and rendered using Jinja's safe filter. Visiting the product page executes HTML/script-capable review content in every viewer's browser.
evidence: products.py:82-91 accepts and stores body without HTML sanitization; product.html:13 renders {{ r.body|safe }}. The same template also explicitly bypasses escaping for this attacker-controlled stored value.

title: Trailing-slash admin refund route bypasses staff authorization
description: Authorization is applied by comparing request.path to the set of exact admin route rules. The refund route is declared strict_slashes=False, so /admin/refunds/ reaches the handler but is not equal to the collected /admin/refunds rule. The handler itself has no authorization check, allowing unauthenticated refunds.
evidence: __init__.py:26-41 checks only exact request.path values. admin.py:52 declares /admin/refunds strict_slashes=False and lines 54-67 perform the refund without checking g.user. POST /admin/refunds/ with no Authorization header returned HTTP 200 {"ok":true,"refunded_pence":1}.

title: Token refresh accepts unsigned attacker-chosen JWT claims
description: The refresh endpoint decodes the submitted JWT with signature verification disabled, then trusts its sub claim to select an account and issues a valid signed token. Anyone who knows or guesses a user ID can mint a session token without a password or valid JWT signature.
evidence: auth.py:100 calls jwt.decode(token, options={"verify_signature": False}); line 104 loads claims['sub'] and line 107 signs a fresh token. POST /auth/refresh with an unsigned token containing sub=3 and an expired exp returned HTTP 200 and a valid staff token.

title: JWT signing key is hardcoded and predictable
description: SECRET_KEY is committed as a fixed source-code value. Anyone obtaining the repository can forge HS256 authentication tokens, including staff-role claims, and the application has no requirement that a deployment override it.
evidence: config.py:3 sets SECRET_KEY = "hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d". auth.py:27 and 42 use this value for all JWT signing and verification.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes
description: Password hashing uses a single unsalted SHA-256 digest, making database compromise vulnerable to rapid offline dictionary/rainbow-table cracking. Password verification also uses a normal equality comparison rather than a password-hashing verifier.
evidence: auth.py:15-20 implements hash_password with hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() and compares the resulting digest directly; registration stores that value at lines 77-78.

title: Payment status timeout fails open as paid
description: If the payment provider times out, the endpoint unconditionally sets status to paid and moves the order to processing. A provider outage or induced timeout therefore lets checkout proceed without confirmation of payment.
evidence: payments.py:37-44 catches requests.Timeout and sets status = "paid" before updating the order to processing and paid_pence = total_pence.

title: CORS reflects arbitrary origins while allowing credentials
description: Every request Origin is reflected into Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and credentials are enabled by default. Any malicious origin can make credentialed cross-origin API requests in browsers if the application uses browser credentials, exposing authenticated responses and enabling state-changing requests.
evidence: __init__.py:44-50 copies the unvalidated Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and emits Allow-Credentials when config enables it; config.py:12 sets CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS = True.
